anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U1 and U12 have both GND1 and GND2 connected to the same single GND net.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver requires its primary and secondary grounds to be separate nets (e.g., logic GND and isolated/bus GND) to provide galvanic isolation; the specification explicitly describes isolated CAN buses using isolated CAN transceivers.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The CAN isolation is defeated; the CAN bus side is not galvanically isolated from the logic ground, so motor-side noise, ground faults, or common-mode transients can reach the CM4/SPI side contrary to the intended isolated CAN architecture.

anomalies.observed: U36 is a SN74LVC1G07 buffer in the e-stop path, but pin 2 (A) does not appear on any net in the netlist.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists U36 as one of the SN74LVC1G07 buffers wired as an e-stop sink gate; its input should be tied to a defined signal or supply so the buffer has a deterministic state.

evidence.quote: U15, U22, U35, U36 (SN74LVC1G07) wired as /OE gates on ESTOP_SINK1/ESTOP_SINK2/ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL

anomalies.impact: The U36 e-stop sink buffer has a floating input, making its output and the downstream U3/U11/U42 e-stop logic undefined or non-functional when U36 is enabled.

anomalies.observed: NET0207 connects only the anodes of D23, D33, and D39; it is not connected to +3V3, +5V, or any other supply/source.
anomalies.expected: Common-anode indicator LEDs need their common anode connected to a positive supply (or the LEDs must be wired as common-cathode devices) to light; these LEDs are connected through resistors to CM4 active-low/open-collector LED outputs.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet/activity indicator LEDs have no supply reference and will not operate as intended.
